policy.selection: Tools are selected explicitly per named use case. A use case returns only the tools that apply to it, plus the baseline that applies to every use case.
policy.installation: MOZAK never installs, registers, launches, or updates third-party tools. Install and registration steps are reported text for the owner or agent host to run deliberately.
policy.networking: stack catalog, recommend, and check perform no networking, no MCP handshake, and execute no external program.
policy.credentials: Credential values are never read into reports. Only environment variable names and their presence are reported.
policy.readiness: stack check observes at most `configured` from explicit host files. Handshake, service usability, and write grants require a separate agent-host probe and are never inferred.
policy.shipping: Third-party tools are not shipped in the MOZAK payload unless `shipped_by_mozak` is true. Pins record the version observed in primary docs on `verified_at`; they are not a claim that MOZAK tested every host combination.
policy.evidence: Anything a tool retrieves is proposal-only research evidence until the owner separately accepts an input.
policy.workflows: Every research route is an MCP server driven by the agent host. MOZAK ships no runtime research adapter and no adapter fallback. Former source-specific batch automation (weekly arXiv and DAIR.AI digests, MCP registry and GitHub watches, HyperResearch and MONOKL vault snapshots) is replaced by explicit agent-host workflows: the agent issues bounded calls, pages explicitly, and pins exact versions, commits, or URLs. Batch parity with the retired adapters is not claimed.
policy.history: Historical adapter runs, bindings, and recorded evidence remain readable through MOZAK's existing evidence readers. The catalog no longer offers adapters as a route.
policy.spend: A tool that consumes paid credits, for example Firecrawl, is never called for network or credit use without explicit owner consent for that purpose.

readiness_ladder.meaning: No declared executable, skill directory, or host registration was found.
A declared executable is on PATH or a declared skill directory exists under HOME.
An explicit host MCP config or MOZAK adapter binding names the tool.
The agent host completed an MCP initialize and tools/list against the server. Not observable by stack check.
A read-only probe call returned real data, for example a library or search result. Not observable by stack check.
The owner explicitly granted write access for a specific purpose. Never inferred and never blanket.

use_cases.title: Baseline for every MOZAK session
use_cases.summary: Output shaping, Notes capture, and terminal diagrams. Merged into every other use case.

use_cases.title: Literature search and section-level paper reading
use_cases.summary: Search arXiv, read one LaTeX section at a time, export BibTeX, and keep topic watches through the arXiv MCP server. Optionally read the curated DAIR.AI AI-Papers-of-the-Week repository at an exact commit through the GitHub or Fetch MCP server. Weekly digests are explicit agent-host workflows, not automatic.

use_cases.title: Reference library, paper reading, and citations
use_cases.summary: Search and read the owner's Zotero library, extract annotations, and export citations. Requires a real local Zotero data directory or web API credentials.

use_cases.title: Manuscript editing on Overleaf (optional)
use_cases.summary: Read, compile, and with an explicit git token edit an Overleaf project. Needs owner-supplied credentials and is never part of the default stack.

use_cases.title: Released tooling watch
use_cases.summary: Track MCP server releases through exact URLs on the official MCP registry v0 API and public GitHub API pages with the Fetch MCP server (required). The read-only GitHub MCP server optionally adds authenticated repository search, releases, tags, and commit heads. The agent pages explicitly and pins exact versions and commits; unauthenticated GitHub API requests are rate limited. No automatic batch watch.

use_cases.title: Bounded multi-source deep research
use_cases.summary: Search and scrape a bounded set of web sources to markdown with the Firecrawl MCP server, which needs FIRECRAWL_API_KEY and consumes credits only with explicit owner consent. The Fetch MCP server optionally snapshots exact URLs. Replaces HyperResearch and MONOKL vault adapters with an explicit agent-host workflow; results are proposal-only evidence.

tools.name: arXiv MCP server

upstream.warning: An unrelated npm package uses the same name. Do not install with npm, pnpm, or npx.

prerequisites.message: Install uv (provides uvx) or `uv tool install arxiv-mcp-server==0.8.1`.

effects.network: arXiv API and Semantic Scholar for search, source, and citation graph

install: or run without installing: uvx arxiv-mcp-server@0.8.1

claude-code.command: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user arxiv -- uvx arxiv-mcp-server@0.8.1

codex.command: codex mcp add arxiv -- uvx arxiv-mcp-server@0.8.1

probes.handshake: From the agent host, list tools on server `arxiv` and confirm `search_papers`, `get_paper_outline`, and `export_citations` are present.
probes.usable: Call `get_abstract` with paper_id `2404.19756` and confirm metadata is returned.
probes.write: None. The server writes only its local paper cache.

tools.notes: Read loop: paper id, outline, one section, citations. Results remain proposal-only evidence.

tools.name: Zotero MCP server

prerequisites.alternative_label: web API mode: both env names declared in the matched host server config or process env (values never read)
prerequisites.message: No zotero.sqlite was found (checked ZOTERO_DB_PATH, Zotero prefs dataDir, and ~/Zotero) and web API mode is not declared. Install Zotero 7+ and open it once to create the data directory, set ZOTERO_DB_PATH to the real database, or declare ZOTERO_API_KEY and ZOTERO_LIBRARY_ID for web mode. Without one of these the server can start and complete a handshake but cannot read a library.

effects.network: none in local read mode; Zotero web API in web or hybrid mode
effects.external_writes: only when the owner authorizes writes (authorize-local or web API key)

install: In Zotero 7+: Settings, Advanced, enable `Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero`.
Writes are optional and need a separate owner decision: `zotero-mcp authorize-local` on Zotero 10+.

claude-code.command: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user -e ZOTERO_LOCAL=true zotero -- zotero-mcp

codex.command: codex mcp add zotero --env ZOTERO_LOCAL=true -- zotero-mcp

probes.handshake: From the agent host, list tools on server `zotero`. A successful handshake does not prove a library is readable.
probes.usable: Call a read-only search tool and confirm at least one real library item. An error about a missing database means the prerequisite is unmet, not that the tool is ready.
probes.write: Never assume. Requires an explicit owner grant per purpose.

tools.notes: Handshake can succeed while no database exists, so `configured` never implies `usable`.

tools.name: zotero-cli agent skill
tools.notes: Lower-context alternative to the MCP server for shell-capable hosts. Shares the Zotero MCP config and database prerequisite.

tools.name: Overleaf MCP server

upstream.warning: The PyPI name `overleaf-mcp` belongs to an unrelated project. The entry point is still `overleaf-mcp`.

prerequisites.message: Set OVERLEAF_SESSION in the host server env from the owner's own browser session. MOZAK never reads or stores it.

effects.external_writes: edit, create, delete, and push tools when OVERLEAF_GIT_TOKEN is supplied

install: or run without installing: uvx --from "overleaf-mcp-plus[compile]==0.3.1" overleaf-mcp

claude-code.command: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user -e OVERLEAF_SESSION=<owner supplies> overleaf -- overleaf-mcp

codex.command: codex mcp add overleaf --env OVERLEAF_SESSION=<owner supplies> -- overleaf-mcp

probes.handshake: From the agent host, list tools on server `overleaf`.
probes.usable: Call `list_projects`. An auth error means the session cookie is missing or expired.
probes.write: Edit and push tools need OVERLEAF_GIT_TOKEN and a separate owner grant for the exact project.

tools.notes: Optional. Never part of the default stack.

tools.name: Fetch MCP server (MCP reference server)

upstream.warning: Upstream cautions that this server can reach local and internal IP addresses. Point it only at the exact public URLs a workflow names.

prerequisites.message: Install uv (provides uvx) or `uv tool install mcp-server-fetch==2026.8.18`.

effects.network: only the exact URLs the agent passes, for example the official MCP registry v0 API, public GitHub API and raw content URLs pinned to a commit, and named source pages; obeys robots.txt for model-initiated requests

install: or run without installing: uvx mcp-server-fetch@2026.8.18

claude-code.command: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch@2026.8.18

codex.command: codex mcp add fetch -- uvx mcp-server-fetch@2026.8.18

probes.handshake: From the agent host, list tools on server `fetch` and confirm `fetch` is present.
probes.usable: Call `fetch` with url `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?limit=1` and raw true, and confirm a JSON body with a `servers` array is returned.
probes.write: None. The server only reads URLs.

tools.notes: Exact-URL retrieval for tooling-watch (MCP registry v0 pages, public GitHub API release and commit endpoints) and for DAIR.AI or source snapshots at an exact commit. Responses are truncated to max_length; the agent continues with start_index and pages registry results explicitly with the API cursor. Unauthenticated GitHub API requests are rate limited. The agent records the exact URL, version, or commit it read. No automatic weekly batch; results are proposal-only evidence.

tools.name: GitHub MCP server (official, read-only)

upstream.warning: Always run with read-only mode and only the `repos` toolset. Grant the token only public or explicitly chosen repository read scope.

prerequisites.message: Install Docker, or download the v1.14.0 `github-mcp-server` release binary for this platform and verify it against `github-mcp-server_1.14.0_checksums.txt`.
Declare GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in the host server env from an owner-created read-only token. MOZAK never reads or stores it. Without it the use case stays incomplete.

install: or download the v1.14.0 release binary from https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server/releases/tag/v1.14.0 and run `github-mcp-server stdio --read-only --toolsets repos`

claude-code.command: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=<owner supplies> github -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -e GITHUB_READ_ONLY=1 -e GITHUB_TOOLSETS=repos ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:v1.14.0@sha256:7aaeeec9ae4fe9a736d100c1ff0798f3c219b5009e05f5d3945fcacb13cc196b

codex.command: codex mcp add github --env GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=<owner supplies> -- docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -e GITHUB_READ_ONLY=1 -e GITHUB_TOOLSETS=repos ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:v1.14.0@sha256:7aaeeec9ae4fe9a736d100c1ff0798f3c219b5009e05f5d3945fcacb13cc196b

probes.handshake: From the agent host, list tools on server `github` and confirm `search_repositories`, `list_releases`, and `get_file_contents` are present and no create, update, push, or delete tool is listed.
probes.usable: Call `get_latest_release` with owner `github` and repo `github-mcp-server` and confirm a real release is returned. An auth error means the token is missing or invalid.
probes.write: None. Read-only mode is required; no write grant is ever requested through this route.

tools.notes: Authenticated specialist route: repository search by topic or keyword, releases, tags, commit heads, and file contents at an exact ref, including DAIR.AI AI-Papers-of-the-Week at a pinned commit. It cannot read the MCP registry, so it never satisfies tooling-watch alone. Stars and pushes measure attention, not quality. The agent pages explicitly and records exact commits; results are proposal-only evidence.

tools.name: Firecrawl MCP server (official)

upstream.warning: Search, scrape, crawl, and agent calls spend Firecrawl credits. Disable the feedback tools and get explicit owner consent before any network or credit use.

prerequisites.message: Declare FIRECRAWL_API_KEY in the host server env from the owner's Firecrawl account. MOZAK never reads or stores it. Without it deep-research stays incomplete.

effects.network: api.firecrawl.dev (or FIRECRAWL_API_URL) plus the pages it searches and scrapes
effects.credit_use: every search, scrape, crawl, and agent call consumes credits on the owner's account and needs explicit owner consent
effects.external_writes: account-side crawl, agent, and monitor jobs only if those tools are called; this route uses search and scrape only

install: Run pinned without a global install: npx -y firecrawl-mcp@3.27.3 (with FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1, FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1 in the host server env)

claude-code.command: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user -e FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=<owner supplies> -e FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1 -e FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1 firecrawl -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp@3.27.3

codex.command: codex mcp add firecrawl --env FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=<owner supplies> --env FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1 --env FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1 -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp@3.27.3

probes.handshake: From the agent host, list tools on server `firecrawl` and confirm `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_scrape` are present. Listing tools spends no credits.
probes.usable: Only after explicit owner consent to spend credits: call `firecrawl_search` with one owner-chosen query and a small limit, and confirm real results. An auth error means the key is missing or invalid.
probes.write: None. Crawl, agent, interact, and monitor tools are out of scope for this route.

tools.notes: Bounded multi-source research: a few owner-approved searches with explicit limits, then scrape of chosen URLs to markdown. Replaces HyperResearch and MONOKL vault adapters with an explicit agent-host workflow, not an automatic vault run. Results are proposal-only evidence with each source URL recorded.
